scenes.script_line: You've completed your story. Congratulations. You've given yourself the gift of bringing your story into alignment, and that is no small thing. So, what now? First, follow through on what you committed to in steps nine and ten. Your rituals and your accountability are what carry this work beyond today. Second, keep your new story where you'll see it. Print a copy and put it next to your mirror, or somewhere you'll connect with it every day, for the next forty-five to ninety days. As you read it, don't just read the words. Let yourself see and feel yourself living inside it. Notice what it's li

scenes.script_line: Here's a simple way to think about why this works. Beliefs are frozen thoughts about yourself and your life. Stories are built from these beliefs, patterns of thought that have become fixed over time. When you shift a story, you begin to loosen what has been frozen. You create movement where there was stagnation, and space for something new to take shape.

shots.text: close-up of a hand tracing a sentence slowly on a page
person sitting quietly, a settled, open expression

scenes.script_line: There will be days when the old story comes back. That's not failure. Old stories are familiar, and familiar things knock on the door. When it happens, go back to your evidence from step six. Re-read your new story. And take one small action that fits it. Each time you do, the new story grows stronger.

shots.text: person pausing, an old doubt crossing their face briefly
person reopening their workbook to a familiar page
person taking one small confident action right after

scenes.script_line: And this is just one story. You can return to this process again and again, across the other areas of your life. Be intentional and courageous about it. Because the sum of all your stories becomes the life you live. The more of them that are true and supportive, the more freely you'll move toward who you're meant to be.

scenes.script_line: Thank you for doing this work with honesty. Before you leave today, take one more look at your new story. Read one line that matters most to you. And carry that line with you into the week ahead. Your facilitator will now close the session with you.
